blocks.content: Parliament shall have the power to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.

rows: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution based on domicile and birth/residence
Citizenship rights of persons who migrated from Pakistan to India
Citizenship rights of migrants to Pakistan who later returned to India under a permit
Citizenship rights of Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) residing outside undivided India
Termination of Indian citizenship upon voluntary acquisition of foreign state citizenship
Guarantees continuance of citizenship rights subject to any law made by Parliament
Empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law

items: Article 9 is frequently asked in exams because it prohibits dual citizenship and enforces mandatory termination of Indian citizenship upon acquiring foreign citizenship.
State Legislatures have zero power over citizenship legislation; Article 11 grants exclusive power to the Union Parliament.
July 19, 1948, is the crucial cut-off date mentioned under Article 6 for persons migrating from Pakistan to India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Part II of the Indian Constitution explicitly deals with citizenship provisions under Articles 5 to 11.
Article 5 grants citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution based on domicile, birth, or residency.
Article 9 establishes the rule of Single Citizenship, automatically terminating Indian citizenship if a foreign nationality is voluntarily acquired.
Article 11 confers supreme authority upon Parliament to enact, alter, or terminate citizenship laws.
